data.title: Histoglobulin (Histoglob PFS)
data.summary: IV Immunotherapy · Human normal immunoglobulin + histamine dihydrochloride combination (non-specific immunotherapy / 'histaminopexy')
data.body:
_Injectables · IV Immunotherapy_

**Class:** Human normal immunoglobulin + histamine dihydrochloride combination (non-specific immunotherapy / 'histaminopexy')

## Mechanism of action
- The histamine–immunoglobulin complex is thought to stimulate antibodies that bind histamine
- This raises the blood's capacity to bind and neutralise free histamine (histaminopexy) and lowers responsiveness to histamine
- May also reduce IgE levels and eosinophil counts and dampen mast-cell activation
- Exact mechanism is not fully established

## Pharmacokinetics
- Given by subcutaneous injection; effect builds over the induction course

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic spontaneous urticaria not controlled with antihistamines (adjunct)
- Allergic rhinitis, allergic asthma (adjunct)
- Atopic dermatitis (limited evidence)

## Dose & formulations
- One prefilled syringe (PFS) subcutaneously per dose
- Induction: 6 injections at 4-day intervals (days 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 as in the manufacturer's calendar); more injections may be given depending on response
- Maintenance: booster doses at 1, 3 and 6 months
- Continue the patient's antihistamine and taper it according to response

## Adverse effects
- Pain, redness or swelling at the injection site
- Fever, headache, transient flare of itch or urticaria
- Rare: hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis (contains human immunoglobulin) — observe after injection
- Blood-product precautions: very small theoretical risk of transmissible infection

## Contraindications
- Known hypersensitivity to human immunoglobulin or histamine
- IgA deficiency with anti-IgA antibodies
- Acute febrile illness or infection (postpone), uncontrolled asthma attack
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding (insufficient data)

## Drug interactions
- Systemic corticosteroids may blunt the response (some prescribing information advises against simultaneous use)
- Live vaccines: immunoglobulin may reduce response — space as per immunoglobulin guidance

## Monitoring
- Urticaria activity score (UAS7) at baseline and follow-up
- Observe 15–30 min after each injection

## Pregnancy & lactation
No adequate data — avoid.

## Viva points
- Histamine + human immunoglobulin → histaminopexy
- Schedule: 6 SC injections every 4 days, then boosters at 1, 3 and 6 months
- Evidence is limited (small studies); guideline step-up for chronic urticaria is antihistamine updosing → omalizumab → cyclosporine

## Note on sources
Histoglobulin is in neither book. The dosing follows the Histoglob PFS card you shared (6 injections 4 days apart, then boosters at 1, 3 and 6 months).

_Sources: Not covered in Wolverton or Khopkar; Histoglob PFS prescribing information (Bharat Serums and Vaccines) and dosing card shared by the user. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
